【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.-The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, frame Effects: The visual frame effects.-"colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, frame Version: The version of the card frame style.-"1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015]),
(hand:TEXT, : The starting maximum hand size total modifier.-A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, has Alternative Deck Limit: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck.-0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, has Content Warning: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information.-0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasFoil:INTEGER, has Foil: If the card can be found in foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasNonFoil:INTEGER, has Non Foil: If the card can be found in non-foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isAlternative:INTEGER, is Alternative: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isFullArt:INTEGER, is Full Art: If the card has full artwork.-0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, is Online Only: If the card is only available in online game variations.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, is Oversized: If the card is oversized.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, is Promotion: If the card is a promotional printing.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isReprint:INTEGER, is Reprint: If the card has been reprinted.-0: has not 1: has not been, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isReserved:INTEGER, is Reserved: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window)-If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStarter:INTEGER, is Starter: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStorySpotlight:INTEGER, is Story Spotlight: If the card is a Story Spotlight card.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTextless:INTEGER, is Text less: If the card does not have a text box.-0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTimeshifted:INTEGER, is Time shifted: If the card is time shifted-If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion., Examples: [0, 1]),
(keywords:TEXT, : A list of keywords found on the card.-, Examples: [First strike, Flying, First strike,Flash]),
(layout:TEXT, : The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"-, Examples: [normal, aftermath, split]),
(leadershipSkills:TEXT, leadership Skills: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in-),
(life:TEXT, : The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.-, Examples: [-5, -1, 2]),
(loyalty:TEXT, : The starting loyalty value of the card.-Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown, Examples: [6, 3, 4]),
(manaCost:TEXT, mana Cost: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value.-manaCost is unconverted mana cost, Examples: [{5}{W}{W}, {4}{W}, {3}{W}]),
(mcmId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [16165, 16166, 16171]),
(mcmMetaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [156, 176, 368]),
(mtgArenaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [74983, 74986, 74987]),
(mtgjsonV4Id:TEXT, : -, Examples: [ad41be73-582f-58ed-abd4-a88c1f616ac3]),
(mtgoFoilId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27501, 26993, 27473]),
(mtgoId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27500, 26992, 27472]),
(multiverseId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [130550, 129465, 129470]),
(name:TEXT, : The name of the card.-Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter., Examples: [Ancestor's Chosen, Angel of Mercy, Aven Cloudchaser]),
(number:TEXT, : The number of the card-, Examples: [1, 2, 7]),
(originalReleaseDate:TEXT, : original Release Date-The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions., Examples: [2012/12/1, 2006/12/1, 2007/12/1]),
(originalText:TEXT, : original Text-The text on the card as originally printed.),
(originalType:TEXT, : original Type-The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes., Examples: [Creature - Human Cleric]),
(otherFaceIds:TEXT, : other Face Ids-A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces., Examples: [87f0062a-8321-5c16-960e-a12ce1df5839]),
(power:TEXT, : The power of the card.-∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(printings:TEXT, : A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.-),
(promoTypes:TEXT, promo Types: A list of promotional types for a card.-"arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork", Examples: [boxtopper,boosterfun, boosterfun, release,buyabox]),
(purchaseUrls:TEXT, purchase Urls: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.-),
(rarity:TEXT, : The card printing rarity.-, Examples: [uncommon, common, rare]),
(scryfallId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [7a5cd03c-4227-4551-aa4b-7d119f0468b5]),
(scryfallIllustrationId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [be2f7173-c8b7-4172-a388-9b2c6b3c16e5]),
(scryfallOracleId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [fc2ccab7-cab1-4463-b73d-898070136d74]),
(setCode:TEXT, Set Code: The set printing code that the card is from.-, Examples: [10E, 2ED, 2XM]),
(side:TEXT, : The identifier of the card side.-Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card., Examples: [a, b, c]),
(subtypes:TEXT, : A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.-, Examples: [Human,Cleric, Angel, Bird,Soldier]),
(supertypes:TEXT, super types: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash.-list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes, Examples: [Legendary, Basic, Legendary,Snow]),
(tcgplayerProductId:TEXT, tcg player ProductId: -, Examples: [15032, 15033, 15045]),
(text:TEXT, : The rules text of the card.-),
(toughness:TEXT, : The toughness of the card.-, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(type:TEXT, : The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes.-"Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant", Examples: [Creature — Human Cleric]),
(types:TEXT, : A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.-, Examples: [Creature, Instant, Enchantment]),
(uuid:TEXT, : The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.-, Examples: [00010d56-fe38-5e35-8aed-518019aa36a5]),
(variations:TEXT, : -, Examples: [b7c19924-b4bf-56fc-aa73-f586e940bd42]),
(watermark:TEXT, : The name of the watermark on the card.-, Examples: [set (HOU), set (LGN), set (ONS)])
]

【DB_ID】 card_games
【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to identify the card with the 'abzan' watermark. Then, I need to find the foreign name associated with that card and its type. The watermark is in the cards table. The foreign name is in the foreign_data table and the type is in the cards table. The uuid is needed to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T2.name, T1.type FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE LOWER(T1.watermark) LIKE '%abzan%'

【DB_ID】 card_games
【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.-The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, frame Effects: The visual frame effects.-"colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, frame Version: The version of the card frame style.-"1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015]),
(hand:TEXT, : The starting maximum hand size total modifier.-A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, has Alternative Deck Limit: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck.-0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, has Content Warning: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information.-0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasFoil:INTEGER, has Foil: If the card can be found in foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasNonFoil:INTEGER, has Non Foil: If the card can be found in non-foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isAlternative:INTEGER, is Alternative: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isFullArt:INTEGER, is Full Art: If the card has full artwork.-0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, is Online Only: If the card is only available in online game variations.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, is Oversized: If the card is oversized.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, is Promotion: If the card is a promotional printing.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isReprint:INTEGER, is Reprint: If the card has been reprinted.-0: has not 1: has not been, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isReserved:INTEGER, is Reserved: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window)-If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStarter:INTEGER, is Starter: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStorySpotlight:INTEGER, is Story Spotlight: If the card is a Story Spotlight card.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTextless:INTEGER, is Text less: If the card does not have a text box.-0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTimeshifted:INTEGER, is Time shifted: If the card is time shifted-If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion., Examples: [0, 1]),
(keywords:TEXT, : A list of keywords found on the card.-, Examples: [First strike, Flying, First strike,Flash]),
(layout:TEXT, : The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"-, Examples: [normal, aftermath, split]),
(leadershipSkills:TEXT, leadership Skills: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in-),
(life:TEXT, : The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.-, Examples: [-5, -1, 2]),
(loyalty:TEXT, : The starting loyalty value of the card.-Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown, Examples: [6, 3, 4]),
(manaCost:TEXT, mana Cost: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value.-manaCost is unconverted mana cost, Examples: [{5}{W}{W}, {4}{W}, {3}{W}]),
(mcmId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [16165, 16166, 16171]),
(mcmMetaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [156, 176, 368]),
(mtgArenaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [74983, 74986, 74987]),
(mtgjsonV4Id:TEXT, : -, Examples: [ad41be73-582f-58ed-abd4-a88c1f616ac3]),
(mtgoFoilId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27501, 26993, 27473]),
(mtgoId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27500, 26992, 27472]),
(multiverseId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [130550, 129465, 129470]),
(name:TEXT, : The name of the card.-Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter., Examples: [Ancestor's Chosen, Angel of Mercy, Aven Cloudchaser]),
(number:TEXT, : The number of the card-, Examples: [1, 2, 7]),
(originalReleaseDate:TEXT, : original Release Date-The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions., Examples: [2012/12/1, 2006/12/1, 2007/12/1]),
(originalText:TEXT, : original Text-The text on the card as originally printed.),
(originalType:TEXT, : original Type-The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes., Examples: [Creature - Human Cleric]),
(otherFaceIds:TEXT, : other Face Ids-A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces., Examples: [87f0062a-8321-5c16-960e-a12ce1df5839]),

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the foreign name and the type of a card that has an 'abzan' watermark. I need to find the card based on its watermark, then retrieve its foreign name and type. The 'cards' table contains the 'watermark' and 'type' columns. The 'foreign_data' table contains the 'name' which represents the foreign name. I will need to join 'cards' and 'foreign_data' on their common 'uuid' column (implied by the foreign key definition).

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, T2.type FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE LOWER(T2.watermark) LIKE '%abzan%'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter cards by set name 'Coldsnap', 2) Filter for cards with faceConvertedManaCost > 5, 3) Filter for cards with unknown power (power = '*'). The name column in the sets table is needed to identify the set. The faceConvertedManaCost column in the cards table is needed to filter for cards with converted mana cost higher than 5. The power column in the cards table is needed to filter for unknown power.

The question asks to count cards from a specific set ('Coldsnap') with a converted mana cost greater than 5 and an unknown power. I need to join the 'cards' table with the 'sets' table to filter by set name. The 'cards' table contains 'faceConvertedManaCost' for filtering mana cost, and 'power' to identify unknown power. The 'sets' table contains the 'name' of the set. Therefore, I need 'cards.faceConvertedManaCost', 'cards.power', 'cards.uuid', 'sets.name', and 'sets.code' to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T1.setCode = T2.code WHERE T2.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.convertedManaCost > 5 AND (T1.power = '*' OR T1.power IS NULL)

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the set named 'Coldsnap', 2) Find the Italian translation for the set's name, 3) Find the text ruling of the cards in that set. The set name is needed to filter the sets table. The language is needed to filter the set_translations table. The text ruling is needed to retrieve the Italian text. The code is needed to join sets and set_translations. The text is needed to retrieve the text ruling.

The question asks for the Italian text ruling of cards in the 'Coldsnap' set. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Identify the set with the name 'Coldsnap' from the 'sets' table. 2. Find the 'setCode' for the 'Coldsnap' set. 3. Use this 'setCode' to find the corresponding translations in the 'set_translations' table, filtering for 'Italian' language. 4. Retrieve the 'translation' text for these Italian translations. 5. The 'rulings' table contains rulings, but it doesn't directly link to the set name or translation language. The 'cards' table has a 'uuid' which is a foreign key in 'foreign_data' and 'rulings', suggesting a link between cards and their rulings/foreign data. However, the question specifically asks for 'text ruling' and 'Italian text'. The 'set_translations' table provides 'translation' text and 'language'. The 'sets' table provides the 'name' of the set. The link between sets and cards is implicitly through 'setCode' in 'set_translations' and a card's set. The question asks for 'text ruling', which implies the 'text' column in the 'foreign_data' table, as it's linked to 'cards' and contains ruling text. The 'language' and 'translation' columns in 'set_translations' are crucial for filtering by Italian and getting the translated text. The 'name' column in 'sets' is needed to identify 'Coldsnap'. The 'setCode' in 'sets' and 'set_translations' is the join key. The 'uuid' in 'cards' and 'foreign_data' is the join key for the ruling text. Therefore, I need 'sets.name', 'sets.code', 'set_translations.language', 'set_translations.translation', 'cards.uuid', and 'foreign_data.text'.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.text
FROM foreign_data AS T1
INNER JOIN cards AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
INNER JOIN sets AS T3
  ON T2.setCode = T3.code
WHERE
  T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.language = 'Italian';

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the set named 'Coldsnap', 2) Find the cards in that set, 3) Determine the highest converted mana cost among those cards, 4) Find the Italian names of those cards. The name column in the sets table is needed to filter for the 'Coldsnap' set. The convertedManaCost column in the cards table is needed to determine the highest converted mana cost. The language and translation columns in the set_translations table are needed to find the Italian names. The setCode column in the sets table is needed to join the sets and set_translations tables. The uuid column is needed to join cards and set_translations tables.

The question asks for the Italian names of cards from the 'Coldsnap' set with the highest converted mana cost. This requires joining the `cards` table (to get card names and converted mana cost) with the `set_translations` table (to filter by language and set). The `sets` table is needed to identify the 'Coldsnap' set. Specifically, I need to: 1. Filter `sets` for the name 'Coldsnap'. 2. Join `sets` with `set_translations` on `setCode` to filter for 'Italian' language. 3. Join the result with `cards` on `uuid` to get card details. 4. Find the maximum `convertedManaCost` among these cards. 5. Select the `translation` (Italian name) for cards matching this maximum cost. Therefore, I need `sets.name` to identify the set, `set_translations.language` and `set_translations.translation` to get the Italian names, `cards.convertedManaCost` to find the highest cost, and `cards.uuid` and `sets.code` to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = (SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost) FROM cards AS T4 INNER JOIN sets AS T5 ON T4.setCode = T5.code WHERE T5.name = 'Coldsnap')

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.name
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN sets AS T2
  ON T1.setCode = T2.code
INNER JOIN set_translations AS T3
  ON T2.code = T3.setCode
WHERE
  T2.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T3.language = 'Italian'
  AND T1.convertedManaCost = (
    SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost)
    FROM cards AS T4
    INNER JOIN sets AS T5
      ON T4.setCode = T5.code
    INNER JOIN set_translations AS T6
      ON T5.code = T6.setCode
    WHERE
      T5.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T6.language = 'Italian'
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question asks for the keyrune code of a set given its code. The set code is used to filter the sets table. The keyruneCode is then selected. The sets table contains the set code and keyrune code.

The question asks to list the 'keyrune code' for a set with a specific 'code'. The `sets` table contains the `code` column to filter by and also the `keyruneCode` column which is what we need to select. Therefore, I need to select the `keyruneCode` from the `sets` table and filter by the `code` column.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT keyruneCode FROM sets WHERE code = 'PKHC'

The artist column is needed to retrieve the illustrator's name. The faceConvertedManaCost column is needed to find the highest cost. It filters for cards with `side IS NULL` (no multiple faces), orders by `convertedManaCost` in descending order to find the highest cost, and then limits to 1 to get the artist of the card with the highest mana cost. 1. **Output Requirements:**
   - Must return the artist/illustrator name (text value)
   - Single value (one artist)

2. **Mandatory Filters/Conditions:**
   - MUST filter for cards where side IS NULL (doesn't have multiple faces)
   - MUST identify the card with the HIGHEST converted mana cost (requires a column for this)

3. **Required Operations:**
   - Finding the maximum converted mana cost (MAX function or ORDER BY DESC + LIMIT 1)
   - Identifying the artist/illustrator associated with that card
   - Requires joining or subquery to link mana cost and artist

4. **Completeness Checks:**
   - ✓ Addresses "illustrator" → return artist name
   - ✓ Addresses "doesn't have multiple faces" → side IS NULL filter
   - ✓ Addresses "highest cost of converted mana" → MAX or ORDER BY DESC

5. **Correctness Checks:**
   - Must find the MAXIMUM mana cost (not minimum or average)
   - Must filter for cards with side IS NULL *before* finding the maximum mana cost
   - Must return the artist/illustrator of the card with the maximum mana cost, not just the mana cost itself

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.originalReleaseDate,
  T3.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T3
  ON T1.uuid = T3.uuid
WHERE
  T1.rarity = 'mythic' AND T1.originalReleaseDate = (
    SELECT
      MIN(originalReleaseDate)
    FROM cards
    WHERE
      rarity = 'mythic' AND originalReleaseDate IS NOT NULL
  ) AND T3.status = 'Legal';

FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE

    SELECT
      MIN(originalReleaseDate)
    FROM cards
    WHERE
      rarity = 'mythic'
  ) AND T2.status = 'Legal';

  T1.originalReleaseDate,
  T3.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T3
  ON T1.uuid = T3.uuid
WHERE
  T1.rarity = 'mythic' AND T1.originalReleaseDate = (

query_selection_reasoning: The query correctly addresses all requirements: it finds the minimum originalReleaseDate for mythic cards, extracts the year (implicitly in the result), and joins with the legalities table to retrieve the legal formats for the card with the oldest release date, filtering for legal status. The output is a list of formats associated with the oldest mythic card.```
query_evaluation_criteria:
1. **Output Requirements:**
   - Must return the release YEAR (single numeric value)
   - Must return a list of LEGAL play formats (multiple text values)
   - Output should be two separate results (year and list of formats)

2. **Mandatory Filters/Conditions:**
   - MUST filter for: rarity = 'mythic' (exact match)
   - MUST identify the card with the MIN(originalReleaseDate)
   - MUST filter for: status = 'legal' (exact match)
   - The format list should be associated with the MIN(originalReleaseDate) card

3. **Required Operations:**
   - MIN function to find the earliest originalReleaseDate
   - Extract the YEAR from originalReleaseDate (or use the year directly)
   - Return the format values for only the cards that match the oldest release date
   - Grouping is not explicitly needed but the result needs to be associated with the oldest mythic card

4. **Completeness Checks:**
   - ✓ Addresses "When was the oldest mythic card released" → MIN(originalReleaseDate) and YEAR extraction
   - ✓ Addresses "what are its legal play formats" → status = 'legal' and format
   - ✓ Addresses "mythic card" → rarity filter
   - All evidence hints are incorporated

5. **Correctness Checks:**
   - "Oldest" refers to MIN(originalReleaseDate), not MAX
   - Year extraction must be from the originalReleaseDate
   - Legal formats must be for the card with the oldest originalReleaseDate
   - Must return a list of formats for the correct card, not all legal formats
   - Must return only legal formats (status = 'legal')

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards, 2) Find the formats of play for the cards illustrated by that artist. The artist column is needed to identify the illustrator. The format column in the legalities table is needed to identify the formats of play. The card's uuid is needed to join the tables.

The question asks for the illustrator (artist) who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for those cards. To find the artist who illustrated the least cards, I need to count the number of cards for each artist. The `cards` table contains the `artist` column, which I can use to group and count. To list the format of play for the cards illustrated by that artist, I need to join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using the `uuid` column, and then filter by the artist identified as illustrating the least cards. The `legalities` table contains the `format` column.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist ORDER BY COUNT(id) ASC LIMIT 1)

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards, 2) Find the formats of play for the cards illustrated by that artist. The artist column is needed to identify the illustrator. The format column in the legalities table is needed to identify the formats of play. The card's uuid is needed to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.artist,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.artist = (
    SELECT
      artist
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      artist
    ORDER BY
      COUNT(uuid) ASC
    LIMIT 1
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to identify sets with Korean translations but without Japanese translations. The set_translations table holds the language translations and the sets table holds set information. I need to filter by language in set_translations and join with sets to get the set names.

The question asks for sets that have Korean translations but do not have Japanese translations. The `set_translations` table contains information about translations, including the language and the set code. To find sets with Korean translations, I need to filter `set_translations` by `language = 'Korean'`. To find sets that *don't* have Japanese translations, I need to check for the absence of entries with `language = 'Japanese'` for a given set. The `sets` table contains the `code` which links to `set_translations` and the `name` of the set, which is what the question asks to list. Therefore, I need `set_translations.language` to filter for Korean and exclude Japanese translations, `set_translations.setCode` to link to the `sets` table, and `sets.name` to list the names of the sets.

The `set_translations` table contains information about translations, including the language and the set code. To find sets with Korean translations, I need to filter `set_translations` by `language = 'Korean'`. To find sets that *don't* have Japanese translations, I need to check for the absence of entries with `language = 'Japanese'` for a given set. The `sets` table contains the `code` which links to `set_translations` and the `name` of the set, which is what the question asks to list. Therefore, I need `set_translations.language` to filter for Korean and exclude Japanese translations, `set_translations.setCode` to link to the `sets` table, and `sets.name` to list the names of the sets.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM sets AS T1 INNER JOIN set_translations AS T2 ON T1.code = T2.setCode GROUP BY T1.code, T1.name HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN T2.language = 'Korean' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN T2.language LIKE '%Japanese%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT

FROM drivers AS T1

  ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId
INNER JOIN races AS T3
  ON T2.raceId = T3.raceId
WHERE
  T1.surname = 'Hamilton' AND T3.year >= 2010;

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT COUNT(T3.raceId)
    FROM drivers AS T1
    INNER JOIN results AS T2
      ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.position > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T2.raceId)
FROM drivers AS T1
INNER JOIN results AS T2
  ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId
INNER JOIN races AS T3
  ON T2.raceId = T3.raceId
WHERE
  T1.surname = 'Hamilton' AND T3.year >= 2010;

WITH RaceDetails AS (
                SELECT
                    T1.raceId,
                    T3.time AS champion_time_str
                FROM races AS T1
                INNER JOIN results AS T3 ON T1.raceId = T3.raceId
                WHERE T1.year = 2008
                  AND T1.name = 'Australian Grand Prix'
                  AND T3.position = 1
                  AND T3.time IS NOT NULL
            ),
            ChampionAndLastTimes AS (
                SELECT
                    RD.champion_time_str,
                    (SELECT T4.time
                     FROM results AS T4
                     WHERE T4.raceId = RD.raceId
                       AND T4.position = (SELECT MAX(position) FROM results WHERE raceId = RD.raceId AND time IS NOT NULL)
                       AND T4.time IS NOT NULL
                    ) AS last_driver_incremental_time_str
                FROM RaceDetails AS RD
            )
            SELECT * FROM ChampionAndLastTimes

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Count the number of matches for each league, 2) Find the league with the maximum number of matches, and 3) Retrieve the league name. The league_id is needed to count matches per league. The name is needed to retrieve the league name. The Match table contains the league_id and the League table contains the league name.

The question asks for the name of the league with the highest number of matches and the count of those matches. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Count the number of matches for each league. The `Match` table contains `league_id` which can be used to group matches by league. 2. Join the `Match` table with the `League` table to get the `name` of the league. 3. Order the results by the count of matches in descending order to find the league with the highest number of matches. 4. Limit the result to the top one. Therefore, I need `League.name` to display the league name, `Match.league_id` to link matches to leagues and count them, and `League.id` to join with `Match.league_id`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.id) DESC LIMIT 1

Count the number of matches for each league. The `Match` table contains `league_id` which can be used to group matches by league. 2. Join the `Match` table with the `League` table to get the `name` of the league. 3. Order the results by the count of matches in descending order to find the league with the highest number of matches. 4. Limit the result to the top one. Therefore, I need `League.name` to display the league name, `Match.league_id` to link matches to leagues and count them, and `League.id` to join with `Match.league_id`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.league_id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.league_id) DESC LIMIT 1

  T1.team_long_name

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to find players with height > 180, calculate their average heading accuracy, and then list the top 10 players by average heading accuracy in descending order. The player_name is needed for the output. The height is needed for filtering players with height > 180. The heading_accuracy and player_fifa_api_id are needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. The player_fifa_api_id is also needed to join the tables.

The question asks to list the names of players whose heights are above 180 and to order them by their average heading accuracy in descending order. Therefore, I need the 'player_name' from the 'Player' table to display the names. The 'height' column from the 'Player' table is needed to filter players whose height is above 180. The 'heading_accuracy' column from the 'Player_Attributes' table is needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. Since the 'Player' table does not contain 'heading_accuracy', and 'Player_Attributes' contains 'heading_accuracy' and 'player_fifa_api_id' which can be used to join with the 'Player' table (assuming a join on player_fifa_api_id is possible, although not explicitly stated in the schema, it's a common practice and implied by the foreign key definition in Player_Attributes referencing Player). Thus, 'player_fifa_api_id' is also needed for the join.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 GROUP BY T1.player_name ORDER BY AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

The 'heading_accuracy' column from the 'Player_Attributes' table is needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. Since the 'Player' table does not contain 'heading_accuracy', and 'Player_Attributes' contains 'heading_accuracy' and 'player_fifa_api_id' which can be used to join with the 'Player' table (assuming a join on player_fifa_api_id is possible, although not explicitly stated in the schema, it's a common practice and implied by the foreign key definition in Player_Attributes referencing Player). Thus, 'player_fifa_api_id' is also needed for the join.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.player_name
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_fifa_api_id = T2.player_fifa_api_id
WHERE
  T1.height > 180
GROUP BY
  T1.player_name
ORDER BY
  AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC
LIMIT 10;

WITH LatestAttributes AS (
  SELECT
    player_api_id,
    crossing
  FROM Player_Attributes
  WHERE
    player_api_id IN (
      SELECT
        player_api_id
      FROM Player
      WHERE
        player_name IN ('Alexis', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone')
    )
  GROUP BY
    player_api_id
  HAVING
    date = MAX(date)
)
SELECT
  T1.player_name
FROM Player AS T1
JOIN LatestAttributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id
ORDER BY
  T2.crossing DESC
LIMIT 1;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find the potential of a specific player on a specific date. The player_name is needed to identify the player. The date is needed to filter the player attributes for a specific time. The potential column is needed to retrieve the player's potential. The player_api_id is needed to join the tables.

The question asks for the 'potential' of a player named 'Francesco Parravicini' on a specific date '2010/8/30'. The 'Player' table contains player names, and the 'Player_Attributes' table contains 'potential' and a date associated with attributes. Therefore, I need to join these two tables on a common player identifier and filter by player name and date to retrieve the 'potential'. The hint specifies 'player_name = 'Francesco Parravicini'' and 'date = '2010-08-30 00:00:00''. However, the provided schema for 'Player_Attributes' does not contain a 'date' column, nor does it have a direct foreign key to 'Player' that includes a date. It seems there might be a missing table or column in the provided schema to link player attributes to a specific date. Assuming there is an implicit link or a missing table that would allow filtering by date, I will proceed with the columns that are present and relevant to the question and hint.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.potential FROM Player_Attributes AS T1 INNER JOIN Player AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T2.player_name = 'Francesco Parravicini' AND T1.date = '2010-08-30 00:00:00'

【DB_ID】 european_football_2
【Schema】
# Table: Player
[
(player_name:TEXT, player name: player name-, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(player_api_id:INTEGER, player api id: the id of the player api-, Examples: [505942, 155782, 162549]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, attacking work rate: the player's attacking work rate-commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low])
]
【Foreign keys】
Player_Attributes.player_api_id=Player.player_api_id
Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id=Player.player_fifa_api_id

This requires the T-CHO column. 3) The ID column is needed to join the tables.

The question asks to list patients born in 1937 with total cholesterol beyond the normal range. To achieve this, I need to: 1) Filter patients based on their birth year being 1937. This requires the 'Birthday' column from the 'Patient' table. 2) Filter patients based on their total cholesterol being greater than or equal to 250. This requires the 'T-CHO' column from the 'Laboratory' table. 3) Join the 'Patient' and 'Laboratory' tables on the 'ID' column to link patient birth dates with their laboratory results. 4) Select the patient ID to list the patients.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) = '1937' AND T2."T-CHO" >= 250

The `Admission` column in the `Patient` table seems to indicate this, and the hint suggests 'in-patient refers to Admission = '+''. 2. Calculate the age of each patient. Filter patients who are 50 years or older. 4. For these filtered patients, I need to retrieve their aCL IgG concentration. This information is in the `aCL IgG` column of the `Examination` table. 5. The question asks for the ID of a patient born on a specific date and whether their alkaliphophatase (ALP) is within the normal range. To find the patient's ID based on their birthday, I need to access the 'Birthday' column in the 'Patient' table. To determine if ALP is within the normal range, I need to access the 'ALP' column in the 'Laboratory' table. Since both tables are linked by the 'ID' column, I will need to join them using 'ID' from both tables. The question also asks for the patient's ID, so the 'ID' column from the 'Patient' table is also necessary.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.ID, CASE WHEN T2.ALP < 300 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END
FROM Patient AS T1
INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2
  ON T1.ID = T2.ID
WHERE T1.Birthday = '1982-04-01'
ORDER BY T2.Date DESC
LIMIT 1;

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH LatestLabs AS (
  SELECT
    ID,
    ALP,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC) AS rn
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE
    ALP IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  T1.ID,
  (T2.ALP < 300)
FROM Patient AS T1
INNER JOIN LatestLabs AS T2
  ON T1.ID = T2.ID
WHERE
  T1.Birthday = '1982-04-01'
  AND T2.rn = 1;

FROM Patient AS T1
INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2

FROM Patient AS T1

The 'type' column in the 'event' table is needed to filter for game events. The 'cost' column in the 'expense' table is needed to calculate the sum of costs. The 'link_to_budget' column in the 'expense' table is needed to join expense with budget table. The 'link_to_event' column in the 'budget' table is needed to join budget with event table.

The question asks for the percentage of the cost for 'game' events. This requires calculating the total cost of game events and dividing it by the total number of game events. The `event` table contains the `type` of event, which is needed to filter for 'Game' events. The `budget` table contains the `spent` column, which represents the cost, and `link_to_event` to join with the `event` table. The hint mentions 'percentage = DIVIDE( SUM(cost), COUNT(event_id)) * 100', implying we need to sum the cost and count the events. However, the schema shows `budget.spent` as the cost and `event.event_id` is not directly available for counting, but `event.type` can be used to identify game events. The `budget` table has `link_to_event` which references `event.event_id`. Therefore, we need `event.type` to filter for 'Game' events and `budget.spent` to sum the costs associated with these game events. The `budget.link_to_event` and `event.event_id` (implicitly through the foreign key) are needed for joining.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT SUM(T3.cost) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.event_id) FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget WHERE T1.type = 'Game'

The question asks for the full name (first_name and last_name, though only first_name is available in the schema) and the college of a club member who holds the position of 'Secretary'.

1.  **Identify the member's name and position:** The `member` table contains `first_name` and `position`. The `position` column will be used to filter for 'Secretary'. The `first_name` column will be part of the output.
2.  **Identify the member's college:** The `member` table has a `link_to_major` column, which is a foreign key to the `major` table. The `major` table contains the `college` name. Therefore, both `member.link_to_major` and `major.major_id` (implicitly, as the FK target) are needed to link members to their colleges. The `major.college` column will be part of the output.
3.  **Join the tables:** To get both the member's details and their college, a join between the `member` and `major` tables is necessary using `member.link_to_major` and `major.major_id`.

Therefore, the essential columns are: `member.first_name`, `member.position`, `member.link_to_major`, `major.major_id`, and `major.college`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name, T2.college FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T1.position = 'Secretary'
